quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: Roche presents new Phase III one-year data for vamikibart (10-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Regulatory: the U.S. FDA accepted Roche's Biologics License Application (BLA) for vamikibart (an investigational intravitreal anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibody) in uveitic macular edema (UME), based on the Phase III MEERKAT and SANDCAT studies; the FDA decision on approval is expected by July 2027. Regulatory submissions have also been filed and accepted in the European Union, China and Japan. Vamikibart has orphan drug designation in the U.S. and EU; if approved, Roche says it would be the first non-steroid targeted treatment for UME.

quarterly_data.quarter: Roche-Genentech press release: Roche presents new Phase III one-year data for vamikibart (10-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Clinical: one-year (52-week) data from the identical Phase III MEERKAT and SANDCAT studies of vamikibart versus sham in UME, presented at AAO 2026: a numerically higher proportion of vamikibart-treated patients achieved vision gains versus sham on the primary endpoint (15 letter or more BCVA improvement), and key secondary endpoints showed sustained improvements in BCVA and central subfield thickness. Approximately two-thirds of eligible patients required no retreatment after 16 weeks, and the majority of those who did required only one additional injection; vamikibart was well tolerated with a low incidence of treatment-related ocular adverse events and intraocular inflammation. CMO Levi Garraway: the results confirm initial visual and anatomical improvements are maintained over 52 weeks.
